dplyr verbs for lazy queries

Source: R/query.R
rcs_query-dplyr.Rd

Methods of the dplyr generics for queries made by store_open(). The verbs are applied by Arrow when the query runs; collect() returns R data (see store_open()), compute() keeps the rows in memory as Arrow data and returns a query on them, pull() collects one column, and glimpse() collects the first rows and shows them.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
filter(.data, ..., .by = NULL, .preserve = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
select(.data, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
mutate(.data, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
rename(.data, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
arrange(.data, ..., .by_group = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
distinct(.data, ..., .keep_all = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
head(x, n = 6L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
collect(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
compute(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
pull(.data, var = -1, name = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
glimpse(x, width = NULL, ...)

Arguments

.data, x

A query made by store_open().

...

Arguments of the dplyr verb.

.by, .preserve, .by_group, .keep_all, width, var, name, n

As in dplyr.

Value

collect(): a tibble or an sf object. pull(): a vector. glimpse(): x, invisibly. Every other verb: an rcs_query.

Details

A filter on partition columns opens only the files of the matching partitions when it comes before any other verb that changes those columns. A pending spatial filter (store_intersects()) applies to the rows of the dataset; its exact test runs in collect() on the rows the query returns, so a head() before collect() may give fewer rows than asked for.
